title: Monsoon and Compass
premise: Storm chaser Gideon Quintana, drowning in debt to the Vane Syndicate's cheerful enforcers, salvages a chest from a flooded river bearing the seal of Meridia—a drowned nation whose treasury was never found. The chest holds a tide-table cipher pointing to the wreck of the Meridian flagship, and every salvage fleet on the coast will kill for it. Dragging her reluctant found family—deckhand Okafor, cartographer Sela, and her estranged half-brother Tomas—into the race, Gideon learns the chest was planted by her dead mother, who once served Meridia's last admiral. At the wreck she discovers the 'treasury' is actually proof that the Syndicate's founder stole Meridia's sovereignty papers to build his empire; choosing to sink the evidence rather than sell it, Gideon pays her debts with truth instead of gold and finally stops running.
about_author: Mara Pemberton is a former hydrographic surveyor who spent six years mapping riverbeds across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who read water the way others read faces.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector Smiles
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Chasing a storm front for salvage fees, she's intercepted by Mr. Lark, the Vane Syndicate's affable collector, who reminds her she owes forty thousand marks and offers one last extension. Emotional beat: dread masked as charm; Gideon realizes running is no longer free.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Dredging after the flood, her winch snags a lead-lined chest stamped with Meridia's sun-and-wave seal. Okafor urges throwing it back; Gideon opens it anyway. Emotional beat: fatal curiosity—the moment staying invisible stops being possible.

chapters.title: Tide-Table Cipher
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. The cartographer recognizes the chest's contents as a naval tide-table encoded in a dead nation's shorthand, pointing to coordinates six tides out. Emotional beat: intellectual thrill curdling into fear as she realizes what everyone else will realize too.

chapters.title: Lark Comes Back Early
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Lark returns with an offer: the Syndicate forgives her debt if she hands over anything Meridian. She lies to his face for the first time. Emotional beat: the vertigo of becoming a liar to survive.

chapters.title: Half-Brother at the Dockside Bar
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Gideon tracks down Tomas, a harbor fixer who sold her out once before, and asks for fleet intelligence. He names his price: a share. Emotional beat: wary reconciliation between two people bound by blood and betrayal.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She lays out the plan: reach the wreck before the salvage fleets mobilize. Okafor refuses, then stays anyway. Emotional beat: the fragile forming of a crew from people with nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: Sela's Map Room Burns
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Someone torches Sela's archive hunting for Meridian charts; she escapes with only what she memorized. Emotional beat: grief for a life's work, hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Optimists
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A flashback chapter: how Gideon borrowed from men who smile while they ruin you, and how her mother vanished leaving only warnings. Emotional beat: understanding that her whole life has been shaped by other people's confidence.

chapters.title: Outrun the Harbor Watch
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The crew slips their aging trawler, the Patient Answer, past port authorities bribed by the Syndicate. Emotional beat: first taste of freedom—and the knowledge that they're now fugitives.

chapters.title: First Tide: The Fleet Wakes
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Radio chatter reveals three salvage fleets are moving; the Syndicate has posted the coordinates' value. Emotional beat: the race becomes real; paranoia sets in among the crew.

chapters.title: Storm Line
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. To lose pursuit, Gideon does what no sane captain would: sails into the storm line she'd normally chase. Emotional beat: exhilaration—her curse becomes her weapon.

chapters.title: Man Overboard
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. A rogue wave sweeps Tomas overboard; Okafor hauls him back against orders. Emotional beat: found family forged in salt water; Tomas begins to earn trust.

chapters.title: Second Tide: The Rival
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They encounter the Corvus, a rival salvage ship captained by Ilsa Reyen, who knew Gideon's mother. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition—Ilsa looks at Gideon like a ghost.

chapters.title: Your Mother Sailed With Us
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Flashback: Gideon's mother, Elena, served aboard a Meridian remnant vessel and entrusted Ilsa with a warning she was to deliver only if Elena died. Emotional beat: the past reaching forward; Gideon learns her mother chose this path for her.

chapters.title: Third Tide: The Warning
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Ilsa delivers Elena's message: 'The chest is bait. What sleeps under the flagship is worse than treasure.' Gideon must decide whether to turn back. Emotional beat: doubt versus momentum; she chooses forward.

chapters.title: Mutiny Weather
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Sela decodes more of the tide-table and finds a second layer—coordinates that don't match the flagship. Someone altered the cipher. Emotional beat: suspicion inside the crew; is there a traitor?

chapters.title: Lark's Patience Ends
chapters.summary: Lark's POV. The Syndicate dispatches the gunboat Perpetual Dawn with orders to take the chest and its finder. Lark requests the privilege of doing it kindly. Emotional beat: menace beneath courtesy; even Lark fears his employers.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide: The Shoals of Names
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Navigating a graveyard of wrecks using Sela's charts, the Patient Answer threads where bigger ships cannot follow—but the Perpetual Dawn is gaining. Emotional beat: skill as survival; Gideon's competence shines.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas is caught passing signals to the Syndicate—not for money, but because they hold his daughter's debts. Emotional beat: shame and confession; the crew votes not to maroon him but to use him.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: False Bottom
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. The second cipher layer resolves: the flagship's cargo manifest lists no gold—only sealed documents in the admiral's strongbox. Emotional beat: dawning comprehension that the real prize is paper, not plunder.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Last Order
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa reveals the final piece: Meridia didn't drown naturally. Its sovereignty was sold out from under it, and the proof went down with the flagship. Emotional beat: history as wound; the scale of the conspiracy emerges.

chapters.title: Perpetual Dawn on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The gunboat appears; Lark hails them with a final offer—surrender the chest, keep your lives. Gideon stalls, buying one tide. Emotional beat: terror managed through performance.

chapters.title: Night Dive
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor and Gideon dive the wreck site in darkness, finding the flagship split on a reef, its strongbox wedged in the engine room. Emotional beat: awe and claustrophobia; touching the drowned past.

chapters.title: The Strongbox
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Inside: Meridia's original sovereignty charter and ledgers proving Vane's grandfather engineered the nation's collapse and bought its remains. Emotional beat: revelation—the Syndicate's fortune is built on a stolen country.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Anchor
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Cornered by the gunboat's arrival, Tomas transmits their position fully, believing resistance means all their deaths. Emotional beat: tragedy of a good man doing the cowardly arithmetic.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Syndicate marines board; the crew scatters the documents' locations through bluff and chaos. Lark finds the chest—empty except for decoys. Emotional beat: desperate improvisation; the family holds together under fire.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide: The Choice
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Captured aboard the Perpetual Dawn, Gideon realizes the documents can buy her freedom—or destroy Vane and restore a dead nation's name. Lark, quietly, tells her which he'd choose. Emotional beat: the moral fulcrum of the book.

chapters.title: What Gold Buys
chapters.summary: Lark's POV. Lark confesses he joined the Syndicate idealistic and stayed comfortable; he warns Gideon that Vane doesn't negotiate, he erases. Emotional beat: unexpected humanity in the enemy; the cost of complicity.

chapters.title: Escape at Slack Water
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Using the slack tide window only she can calculate, the crew turns the tables—flooding the gunboat's lower decks via a hull seam Sela spotted. Emotional beat: triumph through knowledge, not firepower.

chapters.title: Vane Himself
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Aboard the Syndicate flagship, Gideon meets Augustin Vane, urbane and ancient, who offers her everything: debt erased, a fleet, a name. All she must do is hand over the charter. Emotional beat: temptation rendered sincere; power's seduction made personal.

chapters.title: My Mother Refused Too
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Vane reveals Elena Quintana stood in this same cabin and refused the same offer—and paid for it. Gideon understands her mother's disappearance at last. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined—not money, but a choice repeated across generations.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The rescue goes wrong; the Patient Answer burns, Sela is wounded, and the documents nearly go into the sea. Emotional beat: sacrifice—the family pays in blood what they refused to pay in silence.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Holding the charter over open water, Gideon weighs selling it—freedom, wealth, safety—against burning the Syndicate's legitimacy forever. Emotional beat: the climax of conscience.

chapters.title: Sink the Truth
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon seals the charter in the original chest and sinks it beyond any salvage depth, keeping only photographs Sela hid in her charts. Vane's empire now rests on a lie that can surface anytime. Emotional beat: renunciation as victory; she beats him without beating him.

chapters.title: Lark Lets Them Go
chapters.summary: Lark's POV. Ordered to execute the crew, Lark reports instead that the documents are destroyed and worthless—his small rebellion. He tears up Gideon's debt ledger. Emotional beat: grace from an unlikely quarter; complicity broken.

chapters.title: Aftermath at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Shipless and broke, the crew regroups in a harbor tavern. Sela publishes the photographs anonymously to a coastal newspaper. Emotional beat: quiet satisfaction; truth released like a slow tide.

chapters.title: The Empire Cracks
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Over following weeks, Syndicate creditors panic, fleets defect, and Vane's world begins eating itself. Tomas watches his daughter's debt dissolve in the chaos. Emotional beat: vindication; consequences rippling outward.

chapters.title: A New Keel
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The crew pools everything to lay the keel of a new boat—hers, not owed to anyone. Emotional beat: rebuilding; found family made permanent by shared labor.

chapters.title: Elena's Grave
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon visits the unmarked grave Ilsa showed her and finally says goodbye, telling her mother the choice was made and kept. Emotional beat: grief resolved into inheritance honored.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The new ship launches into the first monsoon squall, Gideon at the helm chasing weather not for money but because it's hers to chase. Emotional beat: arrival—at last, stopping costs less than running.
